svg.title: A head injury is a trauma patient first: the primary survey and the Glasgow Coma Scale grade it; a severe injury is acted on for herniation and sent for a STAT CT, which tells epidural, acute subdural, contusion, intracerebral hemorrhage and diffuse axonal injury or traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage apart, each with its own surgical rule; the herniation box names every type, the epidural column carries skull fractures (basilar signs, missed on CT, meningitis risk); a concussion is a clinical diagnosis managed by removal, rest and a graded return, and its column ends with what can follow (second impact, post-concussion syndrome, CTE) and prevention
